chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about Dhu al-Fiqar, the sword of Rasul-Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, from where it was. He said: Jibra'il عليه السلام descended with it from the heaven, and its adornment was of silver, and it is with me.

key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibra'il, the angel who brought it down
key_terms.ذِي الْفَقَارِ: Dhu al-Fiqar, the famed sword of Rasul-Allah صلى الله عليه وآله

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the origin of Dhu al-Fiqar and where it was kept?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Dhu al-Fiqar, the sword of Rasul-Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, was brought down from the heaven by Jibra'il عليه السلام. It also states that its adornment was of silver and that it remained in the possession of the Imam عليه السلام, indicating continuity of the Prophet’s صلى الله عليه وآله sacred relics with the Imams عليهم السلام.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Muhgammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked himasws about Zi Al-Faqar, the sword of Rasool-Allahsaww, from where is it?’ Heasws said: ‘Jibraeelas descended with it from the sky, and its sheath was of silver, and it is with measws’.
en.sarwar: 5. hmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya have narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Hassan from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abdallah who has said that he asked abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.)
about al-Dhulfaqar, the sword of the Messenger of Allah as to wherefrom it was. The Imam (a.s.) said, “Jibril came down with it from the heavens. It was decorated with gold and it is with me now.”
